notes: Pulmonary Embolism Thrombolysis. Intermediate-risk PE (normotensive + RV strain). Thrombolysis reduced hemodynamic decompensation (2.6% vs 5.6%, p=0.02) BUT increased major bleeding + stroke. Risk-benefit unclear for intermediate-risk PE.

Ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis for acute PE. Intermediate-risk PE. USAT improved RV function, reduced RV/LV ratio at 24h (p<0.001). Events 6.7% vs 27.6% (p=0.04). Low-dose lysis option. Small trial.
Massive or submassive PE. USAT reduced RV/LV ratio, improved pulmonary HTN. Low bleeding rate (10% minor, 1% major). Single-arm trial. Established USAT as option for intermediate-high risk PE.
Acute PE treatment. Rivaroxaban non-inferior (2.1% vs 1.8% recurrent VTE, p<0.001 for non-inferiority). Similar bleeding. Single-drug approach simpler. Changed PE treatment - DOACs first-line. NEJM.

Acute VTE (DVT or PE). Apixaban non-inferior for efficacy (2.3% vs 2.7%, p<0.001 for non-inferiority). Major bleeding 69% LOWER (0.6% vs 1.8%, p<0.001). Superior safety profile. Bristol-Myers Squibb/Pfizer. NEJM.

Intermediate-high risk PE. Half-dose tPA reduced clinical deterioration (4.4% vs 8.0%, HR 0.55, p=0.04) with acceptable bleeding. Lower dose safer than full-dose. Targeted thrombolysis approach. ESC 2023.
Intermediate-risk PE. Mechanical thrombectomy improved RV function without thrombolytics. Events 5.8% vs 14.8% (p=0.08). Avoids bleeding from lysis. Emerging PE treatment strategy.
